title: FIND and SEARCH: case-sensitive or not

docs.syntax: =FIND(needle,text) matches case; =SEARCH(needle,text) ignores it; both answer a position
docs.explain:
FIND and SEARCH answer the same question: where inside this text does the needle start. Both count from 1 and both return a position, never the text they found. The only difference is case, and it decides which one you write.

FIND matches case. A code is case-sensitive text, so the hyphen in AN-1042 is found at position 3, and a capital N would not be found in a lower-case label. SEARCH ignores case and finds north, North and NORTH alike.

Use FIND when the character is part of a code and SEARCH when the text was typed by someone else. The wrong choice does not always raise an error: FIND on a label returns #VALUE! only once the cases disagree. The second screen asks for a position in a label, so the function name is what the grader checks.

errors.text: The text you are looking for is not in the cell, and FIND raises #VALUE! instead of returning 0.
SEARCH returns 3 for the hyphen as well, but this screen is graded on FIND, so the answer does not pass.

docs.atWork: Locating a separator or a word inside a code or a label before slicing it.
docs.outcome: Choose FIND for a case-sensitive position, SEARCH when case should not matter.
docs.teaches: FIND reporting a case-sensitive position and SEARCH ignoring case
docs.dataset: Hyphenated codes and typed labels holding lower-case letters

screens.prompt: In B2, report the position of the hyphen in the code in A2.

hints.syntax: =FIND("-",A2): the character first, then the text to search.
hints.func-find: A code is case-sensitive text, so the position comes from FIND.
hints.value: A, N, then the hyphen: third place.
hints.error: The grader reports wrong function if SEARCH appears, even though it also returns 3.

screens.prompt: In B2, report the position of the first N in the label in A2 whatever its case.

hints.syntax: =SEARCH("N",A2): the character first, then the text, with case ignored.
hints.func-search: A label typed by a person can be in any case, so SEARCH is the safe one.
hints.value: b, a, n: the first n is in third place.
hints.error: FIND("N",A2) returns #VALUE! here, because the label holds no capital N.

seo.title: FIND and SEARCH in Excel: case or no case
seo.description: FIND matches capital letters exactly and SEARCH ignores them. Both answer a position counted from the left, which is what makes them useful inside MID.
